note: Everyday items where brand makes no difference. The site says what to look for and how much, with no Budget, Standard and Cadillac tiers (see DECISIONS.md D-06).

items.name: Zip bags, quart and gallon
items.spec: One box of each. They keep documents, clothes, medicines and electronics dry and hold small bits of trash.

items.name: Notebook, pencil and permanent marker
items.spec: A small notebook, two pencils and one marker for labeling and leaving notes.

items.name: Travel-size toiletries
items.spec: Toothbrush, small toothpaste, small soap, and menstrual supplies if needed, for each bag.

items.name: Tissues or a travel roll of toilet paper
items.spec: One pack per bag.

items.name: Small bills and coins
items.spec: Cash in $1, $5, $10 and $20 bills. The site works out an amount on the cash action.

items.name: Spare keys
items.spec: One spare house key and one car key if you have a car, in the bag or with a trusted neighbor.

items.name: Paper plates, cups and utensils
items.spec: Enough for 3 days for 72 hours at home and 14 days for two weeks at home: three plates, three cups and one set of utensils per person per day. They save dishwashing water.

items.name: Toilet paper
items.spec: Count what your household uses in a week and keep at least double that in reserve. About 4 rolls per person per month is a common planning figure.

items.name: Baby wipes or hygiene wipes
items.spec: One large pack (about 70 wipes) per person per week. Never flush them, even when the toilet works.

items.name: Bar or liquid soap and dish soap
items.spec: One spare of each beyond what is in use.

items.name: Paper towels and a few rags
items.spec: Two rolls for 72 hours at home, six for two weeks.

items.name: Ordinary kitchen trash bags
items.spec: One extra roll. These are for household trash, not for toilet waste.

items.name: Matches or a lighter in a zip bag
items.spec: For households with a gas stovetop that needs lighting by hand when the power is off. Never for candles as room light, and never if you smell gas.

items.name: Towels for door gaps
items.spec: Old bath towels kept aside for sealing door gaps against smoke, cold or outside air.

items.name: Books, cards and games
items.spec: A deck of cards, a board game, a few books, paper and pencils. Long outages are boring, and boredom is harder on children.

items.name: Comfort food
items.spec: A small stock of the treats your household actually likes that keep without a fridge.

items.name: Powdered drink mix, tea or instant coffee
items.spec: Makes stored water easier to drink.

items.name: Aluminum foil and oven mitts
items.spec: One roll and one pair, kept with whatever you use to heat food.

items.name: Sunscreen and insect repellent
items.spec: One of each, in date.

items.name: Baking soda
items.spec: Two boxes, for odor in waste and trash cans.

items.name: Clothesline and clothespins, or a folding rack
items.spec: For drying hand-washed clothes indoors or on a balcony.

items.name: Pet waste bags and litter
items.spec: Your pet's usual supplies for the level's number of days.

items.name: Diaper cream and spare pacifiers
items.spec: The brands your baby already uses.
